Subject: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (RAG eval)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Key takeaways:
- Goal: Replace current in-house search + heuristic ranking for customer KB answers with an end-to-end RAG pipeline that reduces incorrect/unsupported answers (hallucinations) and improves F1 for our targeted QA set.
- Priority metrics: grounding rate (fraction of answers citing a document), precision@1 on curated prompt set, and latency SLAs for web autocomplete flows.
- Constraints: want to keep 95th pct latency < 400ms for single-turn lookups; prefer to avoid heavy infra changes in Q1.

Redwood preliminary fit / model recommendations (based on today's dataset size & initial eval requests):
- Retriever: dense bi-encoder for fast recall (we recommend starting with 768-d desktop-tuned bi-encoder).
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for top-10 re-ranking. Candidate: "cross-encoder-reranker-v1" (good precision tradeoff).
- Generator / LM: Redwood-2.9B (q4) for low-latency baseline; Llama-3-13B (fp16) for higher-quality generation if budget allows.

Suggested eval configuration to run next (we can run this and share dashboard):
- Chunking: 512-token source chunks with 256-token overlap
- Retriever top_k: 100 (for recall sensitivity analysis)
- Reranker top_k: 10 (A/B candidate: 5 vs 10)
- Grounding threshold: 0.6 similarity + reranker score threshold (metrics: grounding_rate, precision@1, recall@5)

Attachments + links:
- Attached: prompt_sets_v2.md (the prompt set we used during the call), acme_rag_benchmark_20270207.csv (prelim eval rows)
- Eval dashboard: https://redwood-console.example.com/eval/acme-rag-2027 (short link also attached)

Immediate next steps I suggest:
1) Redwood runs the retrieval + reranker sweep with the config above and shares the dashboard by EOD Wed (02/09).
2) Joint review session (30–45m) to go over results and decide A/B plan for reranker at top_k=5 vs 10 — propose Thu 02/10 or Fri 02/11.
3) If satisfied, we'll draft a scoped pilot (traffic %, cost estimate, rollout plan).

Can you confirm the metrics you want in the dashboard (I included grounding_rate & precision@1 — anything else?) and what date/time works for a quick review?

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi all — adding technical context and a proposed plan for the sweep. 

Quick answers to Sam's questions and proposed experiments: 
- Grounding threshold: 0.6 is a sensible starting point. In our prior customers we see that 0.6 + cross-encoder rerank reduces unsupported assertions to ~3-6% depending on KB cleanliness. We'll include a hallucination metric (unfounded_answer_rate) in the dashboard so you can see the distribution.

- Bi-encoder-only vs bi-encoder + cross-encoder: 
  * Bi-encoder-only (fast): good recall, very low CPU on rerank stage, but weaker final precision (more false positives). Useable if tight latency budgets — we've seen acceptable precision for internal KB if top_k retriever <= 20 and strong embedding model.
  * Bi-encoder + cross-encoder (recommended): higher precision because cross-encoder models examine query+doc pairs. Costs: extra compute and latency proportional to reranker_top_k (we recommend 5-10).

Proposed sweep (we'll run and push results to the dashboard):
- Retriever model: dense 768-d bi-encoder (faiss index)
- Chunk size: 512 / overlap 256
- Retriever top_k values to test: 20, 50, 100
- Reranker variants: none (bi-only), cross-encoder small (cross-encoder-reranker-v1), cross-encoder-large (cross-encoder-reranker-v2)
- Reranker top_k to test: 5, 10
- Metrics: grounding_rate (percent answers with doc refs), precision@1, recall@5, latency_p95, unfounded_answer_rate (hallucination proxy)

Preliminary latency estimates (approx):
- Bi-encoder-only (top_k=20): p95 ~ 180-250ms (depends on caching and batching)
- Bi-encoder + cross-encoder (top_k=10, cross-encoder-v1): p95 ~ 320-420ms
- Cross-encoder-large: p95 ~ 450-600ms (likely outside your 400ms goal)

Given your 400ms p95 target, our recommended A/B for the pilot:
A) Bi-encoder + small cross-encoder (top_k=5, reranker_top_k=5) — best precision/latency balance
B) Bi-encoder-only (top_k=20) — best latency/cost balance

I attached the raw CSV with the preliminary run (acme_rag_benchmark_20270207.csv) and a pointer to the dashboard. We'll push the full sweep by EOD Wed (02/09).

Planning note: Rachel — can you help prepare a short one-sheet that maps metric thresholds to rollout gates (e.g., unfounded_answer_rate < 5% => proceed to 10% traffic)?

Thanks,
Priyom
